name: Thoracic Outlet Venous Syndrome
definition: Compression of the subclavian vein at the thoracic outlet, potentially causing effort thrombosis (Paget-Schroetter syndrome).

investigations.principle: Duplex ultrasound and venous cross-sectional/contrast imaging are used according to vascular pathway.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, vascular, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

green: Urgent vascular assessment when thrombosis is suspected
amber: Anticoagulation, thrombolysis and decompression decisions are specialist-directed.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Rakta-vaha/upper-limb swelling phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Compression of the subclavian vein at the thoracic outlet, potentially causing effort thrombosis (Paget-Schroetter syndrome).
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
